Where an account stands with the platform.

Only SUSPENDED and CLOSED stop a person transacting outright. RECOVERY and COOLDOWN are
temporary states a person passes through on their way back to ACTIVE, which is why they
are separate values rather than flags on an active account.
AccountStatus.title: AccountStatus

the same arithmetic holds whichever side is chosen, and only the split moves. It is a
string enum so that the setting can be written `SPLIT_50` in an environment variable and
stored in that form, without a mapping table translating it on the way in.

ListingCreateBody.description:
A listing as a seller states it.

Everything here is what the seller knows at the moment of posting. What the platform
adds around it — the source it arrived through, the status it starts in, the short code
it is quoted by — is not accepted from the client, because a client that could set its
own status could also set a listing that was never reviewed.

``expires_at`` is optional because a listing that nobody thought about should still be
postable: thirty days is the default the specification gives.

``on_behalf_of_user_id`` is the one field here that is not the seller's own hand. When it
is present the request is a delegated posting: the caller must be an agent holding an
active assignment for that farmer, the listing's seller becomes the farmer, and this field
names whose behalf it was posted on. An ordinary seller never sends it, and sending it
without the assignment is refused rather than ignored.

on_behalf_of_user_id.description: Post this listing as another account, whose behalf an agent is acting on. Requires an active agent assignment for that account.
on_behalf_of_user_id.title: On Behalf Of User Id

ListingCreateBody.title: ListingCreateBody

ListingResponse.description:
A listing as it is read back.

The seller's own point on the map is not here, and neither is which account an agent
wrote on another's behalf. Everything published about a listing is what a buyer needs in
order to decide whether to buy it.
ListingResponse.title: ListingResponse

ListingStatus.description:
Where a listing sits in its life.

The transitions between these are not free; they are the state table, and one guard in
the service layer decides which of them are allowed.
ListingStatus.title: ListingStatus

ListingUpdateBody.description:
A change to some of a seller's own listing.

A merge, so an absent field means leave it alone. That is why a nullable field cannot be
unset by omitting it: clearing one is an explicit value, and this slice does not offer a
way to tell "absent" from "empty" for text. ``version`` is required, because an edit
that is not sure what it is editing is how two phones overwrite each other.

Not editable here, deliberately: ``status`` moves only through the lifecycle endpoints,
``short_code`` is quoted to buyers already and cannot be changed under them, ``sold_kg``
is written by orders rather than by their seller, and the crop, the region and the woreda
are what the listing is an offer *of*, *where* and *in*. Those four have no field here at
all rather than a field that is quietly ignored, so a client that tries finds out.
ListingUpdateBody.title: ListingUpdateBody

OfferCounterBody.description:
A seller's answer to an open offer, on different or the same terms.

The same terms as an opening bid on purpose. A counter is a new offer with new terms, and
holding it to the same bounds as an opening bid is what stops an answer from being a way to
propose something an opening bid could not have proposed. What it deliberately does *not*
carry is a payment mode: a counter keeps the mode of the offer it answers, so how a sale
would be paid for is chosen when the thread opens and cannot be changed by answering. A body
that tried anyway is refused by the inherited `extra="forbid"`.
OfferCounterBody.title: OfferCounterBody

OfferCreateBody.description:
The terms a buyer is bidding, and the mode they are bidding on.

Only what is relative to the listing is left out: the ceiling of twice the asking price and
the weight floor of the listing's minimum order are both rules about a listing this request
does not carry, so they are checked where the listing is read.
OfferCreateBody.title: OfferCreateBody

OfferResponse.description:
An offer as it is read back.

`status` is the derived one, so an offer whose window has closed reads as expired rather
than as a standing bid nobody has answered. `proposed_by` is derived from the depth for the
same reason: a client deciding what it may do next needs to know whose turn it is.
OfferResponse.title: OfferResponse

OfferStatus.description:
Where an offer sits in its own short life.

Only `OPEN` has anywhere to go. Everything else is a record of how the negotiation ended,
and a record of that kind is not edited, reopened or renegotiated — a superseded bid is not
a bid anybody may return to, it is what the counter that replaced it was an answer to.
OfferStatus.title: OfferStatus

OrderAcceptBody.description:
Where the goods go, on an acceptance whose price and weight are already settled.

The weight is the offer's and the price is the offer's. Repeating either here would give a
seller two ways to agree to something, and they would disagree the first time the two fields
were filled in differently.
OrderAcceptBody.title: OrderAcceptBody

OrderBuyNowBody.description:
A purchase at the asking price, with the weight the buyer wants.

`payment_mode` defaults to escrow, which is the only mode most deployments offer. A COD
order is the buyer choosing to pay on delivery rather than fund the order, and it is
gated by configuration: a mode the platform has not opened cannot be chosen, no matter
what the body says.
OrderBuyNowBody.title: OrderBuyNowBody

OrderResponse.description:
An order as it is read back.

The money figures are the frozen ones, so a client showing "what I pay" shows what will
actually be taken. `pickup_code` is here because it is the buyer's to keep and the seller's
to ask for — but only to the buyer: the seller's copy of the order does not carry the code
they are supposed to be asking it for, because a code visible to the party being verified is
a code the verification proves nothing about. `cancel_reason` is here because "it expired"
and "I cancelled it" are different things to the buyer looking at a list, and one word for
both would lose that.
OrderResponse.title: OrderResponse

OrderStatus.description:
Where an order sits in its life.

The transitions between these are not free: they are the state table in the service layer,
and one guard decides which of them are allowed. `CANCELLED_REFUNDED` is distinct from
`CANCELLED` because a cancelled order never took the buyer's money while a refunded one did,
and an account statement that could not tell those apart would be no statement at all.
OrderStatus.title: OrderStatus

PaymentMode.description:
Whether the platform holds the buyer's money until delivery, or never sees it.

COD orders never move money: both parties confirm the terms instead of the buyer funding
them, and the order stays `CREATED` until that happens. Escrow orders are born
`AWAITING_FUNDING` and stay there until payment arrives. Which settlement path an order
is on is decided by this column, so a reader never has to guess from a missing value.
PaymentMode.title: PaymentMode

The six digits a seller reads back from a buyer at the roadside.

Digits only, because the code is read aloud in a market by somebody who is not typing into
a form. `extra="forbid"` is what keeps a pickup confirmation honest: a code and nothing
else is all this move needs, and a body carrying more is the beginning of a pickup being
confirmed by something other than the code.

FR-405's board for one crop in one region: the published day's five figures.

The three prices are withheld together when the day judged too little to say, which is
what `insufficient_data` carries; an average with no edges beside it, or edges with no
average, would be the very presentation the thin-sample rule exists to refuse.

A change to some of the caller's own fields.

Every field is optional and every field that arrives is applied on its own: this is a
merge, so an absent field means "leave it alone" rather than "clear it".

`gps` is here because the platform accepts it, though the published contract does not yet
list it; it is stored at reduced precision and never sent back.

Proposer.description:
Which side of the negotiation put these terms on the table.

Derived from the depth rather than stored, because the depth already says it and a second
column saying the same thing is a second thing that can be wrong. Even depths are the
buyer's terms and odd depths are the seller's, starting from the fact that a thread begins
with a buyer.

VerificationTier.description:
How much a platform has verified about a person.

Tier 0 is the starting point and requires nothing; higher tiers unlock larger
transactions and faster settlement, so the level is recorded on the account rather
than inferred at request time.
VerificationTier.title: VerificationTier

WeightBody.description:
The delivered weight, in whole kilograms, recorded by the seller.

The upper bound is enforced twice — here by a flywheel that stops a nonsense figure from
reaching the service, and again in the service against the ordered amount (a thousand
kilos ordered can never deliver twelve hundred) — because the first bound is about the
shape of the number and the second is about the trade it belongs to.
WeightBody.title: WeightBody

get.description: Report that the process is serving. Always 200 while it is up.

post.description:
Send a code to the farmer's phone and hand back a handle to the exchange.

Nothing is created here. An account appears only when the farmer — not the agent — proves
the number, which is what the second route does.

Prove the farmer's number, create or recover the account, and record the relationship.

The code is checked against the number the handle carries, never one the caller names, so
the proof is bound to the exchange the agent started. On success the farmer exists, is
linked to the agent for twelve months, and is returned — and nothing else about them is
written by the agent's hand.
Close the session a refresh token belongs to.
Send a verification code to a number.
Exchange a verification code for a session, registering the trader if new.

Trade a refresh token for a fresh pair.

Each refresh token works exactly once. Presenting one that has already been traded
closes every session on the account.

get.description:
FR-405's board, public: what this crop has been costing in this region, or that we
do not know yet.

Public on purpose, and that is a decision rather than an oversight: the board is the
platform's answer to "is this price odd", and a buyer standing in a market with no
account and a farmer checking whether today's offer is fair are exactly who needs to
ask it.

The latest published day is read rather than today's alone, because the aggregation runs
at two in the morning and a board read at dawn is meant to be yesterday's arithmetic -
that is the day it finished. No row at all is not a 404: the board exists and says there
is not yet enough to say, which is the same honest answer a thin row gives, and a reader
learns the same thing either way.

post.description:
Take one signed text message, act on it, and reply by text.

Always answers 200 to a signed, well-formed request, whether the command succeeded or was
refused for a business reason. The reply the trader receives is the result; the gateway is
told only that the message was received.
Answer one keypress with the plain-text screen the network should show.

get.description:
Woredas, narrowed to one region when the caller names one.

Leaving the region out returns everything seeded so far, which is what a caller that
has not narrowed yet wants.

schema.title: Response List Woredas V1 Woredas Get
